title: Chirality, Klein duality, and the stability of Kitaev spin liquids on the star lattice
abstract: The star lattice hosts the Yao-Kivelson chiral spin liquid, an exactly solvable Kitaev spin liquid that breaks time reversal spontaneously and is non-Abelian or Abelian depending on the ratio of its two couplings. A density-matrix renormalization group study found that an added Heisenberg exchange leaves it a wide stability window for ferromagnetic but only a narrow one for antiferromagnetic Kitaev coupling. Using projective symmetry groups (PSGs) of fermionic partons, we show that the chirality is not a peculiarity of the solvable point: whenever the $π$ spin rotations act on the partons as in the exact solution (spin-gauge locking), a time-reversal-symmetric mean-field state has no amplitude on the triangles, at any range, so a Kitaev-type spin liquid on this lattice must break time reversal. The Abelian and non-Abelian liquids of both signs share a single chiral PSG, within which their transition is a band inversion. The Klein duality, which reverses the Heisenberg coupling, permutes the PSGs and leaves exactly the locked ones unchanged; a $Z_2$ spin-liquid phase mapped onto itself is therefore locked and, if it spans a connected range of couplings, contains a Kitaev point. Unprojected mean-field theory in Kitaev's Majorana representation treats both signs alike. Exact second-order perturbation theory about the Kitaev points locates the asymmetry: the triangles respond identically for both signs, whereas on the bonds between triangles the two off-diagonal Heisenberg terms create the same four visons and interfere constructively for antiferromagnetic and almost destructively for ferromagnetic coupling, admixing a low-energy four-vison state $82$ times more strongly on the antiferromagnetic side. The PSG results rest on a classification of $352$ $Z_2$ PSGs with spin-orbit-coupled amplitudes, which also identifies the fermionic partners of the known Schwinger-boson spin liquids.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes Kitaev spin liquids on the star lattice, demonstrating that the system must spontaneously break time-reversal symmetry to realize its chiral state. Using advanced group theory (PSGs) and perturbation theory, the authors map out the stability regimes and show how duality transformations constrain the possible quantum phases.
main_problem: The paper investigates the chirality, Klein duality, and stability of Kitaev spin liquids on the star lattice.
main_result: The analysis shows that the chiral nature of the spin liquid is robust, requiring time-reversal symmetry breaking, and that the system's physics is governed by the interplay between symmetry constraints and duality transformations.
method: The study employs advanced theoretical tools including Density-Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG), Projective Symmetry Groups (PSGs), and exact second-order perturbation theory.
model_or_system: The system is the Kitaev spin liquid model on the star lattice, which is a periodic tricoordinated lattice derived from the honeycomb lattice. The Hamiltonian involves Kitaev and Heisenberg couplings, leading to both Abelian and non-Abelian topological phases.
key_observables: Chirality (spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking), topological order (Abelian vs. non-Abelian), and the energy response to Heisenberg coupling via vison creation.
important_parameters: The ratio of Kitaev to Heisenberg couplings, and the specific values of the couplings ($K, J_t, J_e$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the PSG framework, which classifies $Z_2$ PSGs, and the use of mean-field ansatzes, though perturbation theory helps locate asymmetries beyond these approximations.
figures_summary: The notes reference tables detailing parameters for various lattice configurations (ZCxxxxxx) and summarize the counting of U(1) PSGs across different symmetry sectors.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical model and the role of chirality, to developing the PSG framework for symmetry constraints, analyzing the implications of Klein duality, and finally using perturbation theory to locate coupling asymmetries.
why_interesting: The deep connection between lattice geometry (star lattice), topological order (Kitaev liquids), and fundamental symmetries (chirality, time-reversal) provides a rich theoretical playground for understanding emergent quantum phenomena relevant to strongly correlated materials.
